summary: This Wikipedia article covers Sony Music Entertainment (SME), an American music corporation operated by Sony Corporation of America and descended from the American Record Corporation, later Columbia Recording Corporation and CBS Records. It traces ownership changes, including CBS's 1938 acquisition of ARC, Sony's 1987 purchase and 1991 renaming, the 2004 merger into Sony BMG and Sony's 2008 buyout of Bertelsmann's stake, and leadership changes such as Doug Morris becoming chairman and CEO in 2011. It also describes the history of affiliated labels including Columbia, Epic, Date and Okeh.
one_line: History and corporate evolution of Sony Music Entertainment, from ARC and CBS Records through Sony BMG to its current structure.
key_facts: The American Record Corporation (ARC) was acquired by the Columbia Broadcasting System (CBS) in 1938 and renamed Columbia Recording Corporation.
Ted Wallerstein, an RCA Victor Records executive, convinced CBS head William S. Paley to buy ARC.
Wallerstein restored Columbia's status as a leading record company and spearheaded the successful introduction of the long playing (LP) record before retiring as Columbia's chairman in 1951.
Columbia founded Date Records in 1958, which initially issued rockabilly music.
Date's biggest success was "Time of the Season" by the Zombies, peaking at #2 in 1969; the label was discontinued in 1970.
In 1964, CBS established its own UK distribution with the acquisition of Oriole Records.
In 1986, CBS sold its music publishing arm, CBS Songs, to Stephen Swid, Martin Bandier, and Charles Koppelman for $125 million, making it the foundation of their SBK Entertainment.
In 1987, Sony Corporation of Japan bought the company; in 1991 it was renamed Sony Music Entertainment (SME) on January 1, 1991.
Sony reintroduced the Columbia label worldwide on January 1, 1991, after acquiring the international rights to the trademark from EMI in 1990.
In 2004, SME and Bertelsmann Music Group merged as Sony BMG Music Entertainment.
On August 5, 2008, SCA and Bertelsmann announced that Sony had agreed to acquire Bertelsmann's 50% stake in Sony BMG; the acquisition was completed on October 1, 2008.
Doug Morris, formerly of Warner Music Group and Universal Music, became chairman and CEO of the company on July 1, 2011.
The RCA Music Group closed Arista, J Records and Jive Records in October 2011, moving their artists to RCA Records.
Barry Weiss left as RCA/Jive Label Group CEO in March 2011 to become CEO of Island Def Jam and Universal Republic.
According to the note, SME is the world's second largest recorded music company, after Universal Music Group.
